new.s: Which date did the Supreme Court fix in Waman Rao (1981) as the cut-off for reviewing Ninth Schedule laws?
new.x: Waman Rao fixed 24 April 1973, the date of the Kesavananda Bharati judgment; laws placed in the Ninth Schedule after it are open to challenge.
new.angle: U0295 notes: Waman Rao -> cut-off date

new.s: In which case were free and fair elections and democracy reaffirmed as basic features of the Constitution in 2006?
new.x: Kuldip Nayar v. Union of India (2006) reaffirmed free and fair elections and democracy as basic features.

new.s: Which case of 1987 held the rule of law to be a basic feature of the Constitution?
new.x: P. Sambamurthy (1987) treated the rule of law as part of the basic structure.

new.s: Which case directed compulsory registration of marriages?
new.x: In Seema v. Ashwani Kumar (2006) the Supreme Court directed compulsory registration of marriages.

new.s: Which law did Parliament enact after the Shayara Bano judgment on instant triple talaq?
o: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019
Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (POSH) Act, 2013
new.x: After Shayara Bano (2017), the 2019 Act made instant triple talaq an offence punishable with up to three years in jail.
new.angle: U0296 #4 case -> law enacted in response (2019 Act)

new.s: Which judgment of the Supreme Court dealt with conversion to another religion to contract a second marriage?
new.x: Sarla Mudgal (1995) held that a Hindu husband cannot convert to Islam just to marry again; it also called for a Uniform Civil Code.
new.angle: U0296 PYQ y31f1eb66dca angle: UCC / personal law -> case

new.s: In which case did the Supreme Court read 'equal pay for equal work' from Articles 14, 16 and 39(d)?
new.x: Randhir Singh (1982) drew equal pay for equal work from Articles 14, 16 and 39(d) and the word 'Socialist'.
new.angle: U0296 notes: Randhir Singh -> equal pay

new.s: In which case did the Supreme Court describe the CBI as a 'caged parrot'?
new.x: In the coal allocation case of 2013 the Supreme Court called the CBI a 'caged parrot'.
new.angle: U0296 notes: caged parrot -> coal case

new.s: Who headed the Supreme Court's mediation panel in the Ayodhya case in 2019?
new.x: The panel was headed by Justice F.M.I. Kalifulla, with Sri Sri Ravi Shankar and Sriram Panchu as members.

new.s: Which Constitutional Amendment relating to Andhra Pradesh was struck down in P. Sambamurthy (1987)?
new.x: P. Sambamurthy (1987) struck down the 32nd Amendment provision on the AP Administrative Tribunal.

new.s: Which section of the Aadhaar Act, which allowed its use by private entities, was struck down in 2018?
new.x: The 2018 Aadhaar judgment struck down Section 57, so private entities cannot demand Aadhaar.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Indra Sawhney (1992):
1. It upheld 27% reservation for OBCs.
2. It excluded the creamy layer from reservation.
3. It removed the 50% ceiling on reservations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Indra Sawhney upheld 27% OBC quota and excluded the creamy layer, but it fixed a 50% ceiling; it did not remove it.

new.s: Which doctrine treats the State as the legal protector of citizens who cannot protect themselves?
new.x: Parens patriae means the State acts as guardian of those unable to protect themselves.

new.s: Which principle settles a conflict between a Central law and a State law on the same Concurrent List matter?
new.x: Under Article 254 the Central law prevails (federal paramountcy); pith and substance only decides which List a law falls in.
new.angle: U0297 notes: APPSC G2 2017 area -> federal paramountcy (Art. 254)

new.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that separation of powers in India is functional and not rigid?
new.x: Ram Jawaya Kapur (1955) held that India has no rigid separation of powers.

new.s: From which country does the doctrine of prospective overruling come?
new.x: Prospective overruling comes from the USA; it was first used in India in Golaknath (1967).

new.s:
Match the following:
List-I (Doctrine)
a. Eclipse
b. Waiver
c. Pith and substance
d. Colourable legislation
List-II (Case)
1. Basheshar Nath
2. Bhikaji Narain
3. K.C. Gajapati Narayan Deo
4. F.N. Balsara
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
new.x: Eclipse - Bhikaji Narain; waiver - Basheshar Nath; pith and substance - Balsara; colourable legislation - Gajapati Narayan Deo.

new.s: What does 'constitutional government' mean?
o: Limited government, limited by the terms of the Constitution
Government by a party with a two-thirds majority
Government in which Parliament is sovereign in every matter
Government run by the civil services
new.x: A constitutional government is a limited government whose powers are fixed and checked by the Constitution.

new.s: In India, to which organ is the executive subordinate?
new.x: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, so the executive is subordinate to the legislature.
new.angle: U0298 #3 executive subordinate to which organ

new.s: Which Articles bar courts from questioning the proceedings of Parliament and State Legislatures on the ground of irregular procedure?
new.x: Articles 122 and 212 protect legislative proceedings from court inquiry on procedure; 121 and 211 bar discussion of judges.

new.s: Which of the following elections in India is NOT held by proportional representation by single transferable vote?
new.x: PR-STV is used for the President, Vice-President, Rajya Sabha and Legislative Council; Lok Sabha uses first-past-the-post.
new.angle: U0299 PYQ yef2e90b0786 angle: STV -> which elections

new.s: How are votes cast in the election of the President of India?
new.x: The President is elected by PR-STV through secret ballot.
new.angle: U0299 notes: method of election -> secret ballot

new.s: Who holds the office of President if the successor has not entered office when the five-year term ends?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
new.x: Under Article 56 the outgoing President continues until the successor enters office.
new.angle: U0299 PYQ y76428717b46 angle: delay in election -> outgoing President continues

new.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The President can pardon a death sentence.
2. The Governor can pardon a sentence passed by a court-martial.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Only the President can pardon a death sentence or a court-martial sentence; the Governor cannot.
new.angle: U0299 PYQ y0dfd95f7cf2 angle: death sentence pardon -> only President

new.s: On what ground can the President of India be impeached under Article 61?
o: Loss of confidence of the Lok Sabha
new.x: Article 61 gives only one ground for impeachment: violation of the Constitution.

new.s: In which House can the impeachment charge against the President be initiated?
o: A joint sitting of both Houses
new.x: The charge can start in either House; the other House investigates it.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the impeachment of the President?
o: It is borrowed from the Constitution of the UK
Nominated members of Parliament take part in it
No President of India has so far been impeached
new.x: The impeachment procedure is borrowed from the USA, not the UK.

new.s: Which Constitutional Amendment made the advice of the Council of Ministers binding on the President?
new.x: The 42nd Amendment made the advice binding; the 44th later allowed the President to return it once.

new.s: Within what period must an election be held to fill a vacancy in the office of President caused by death or resignation?
new.x: Article 62(2) requires the election within six months of the vacancy.

new.s: Who acts as President when the offices of both the President and the Vice-President are vacant?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
new.x: Under the President (Discharge of Functions) Act, 1969, the CJI acts, and then the senior-most Supreme Court judge.
new.angle: U0299 #7/#17 vacancy -> who acts in absence of both

new.s: Who was the only Chief Justice of India to act as President?
new.x: CJI M. Hidayatullah acted as President from 20 July to 24 August 1969.

new.s:
Arrange the following Presidents of India in chronological order:
1. Zakir Husain
2. N. Sanjiva Reddy
3. S. Radhakrishnan
4. V.V. Giri
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
new.x: S. Radhakrishnan (1962), Zakir Husain (1967), V.V. Giri (1969), N. Sanjiva Reddy (1977).

new.s: Who among the following Presidents of India was earlier the first Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: N. Sanjiva Reddy of Anantapur was the first CM of AP (1956) and later Lok Sabha Speaker and President.

new.s: Who was the first Dalit President of India?
new.x: K.R. Narayanan (1997-2002) was the first Dalit President; he also won a record share of votes.

new.s: What does the President swear to do in the oath under Article 60?
o: Preserve, protect and defend the Constitution and the law
Bear true faith and allegiance to Parliament
Uphold the sovereignty of the Lok Sabha
Act on the advice of the Prime Minister in all matters
new.x: The President swears to preserve, protect and defend the Constitution and the law; the CJI administers the oath.

new.s: Which Constitutional Amendment froze the 1971 Census as the population base for the Presidential election till the first Census after 2026?
new.x: The 84th Amendment kept the 1971 Census as the base until the first Census after 2026.
new.angle: U0299 #1 value of vote -> population base

new.s: Which Bill did President Giani Zail Singh keep pending by using the pocket veto?
new.x: Zail Singh used the pocket veto on the Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill, 1986, the only use at the Union level.

new.s: Which of the following powers does the Governor NOT have over State Bills?
o: Reserving a Bill for the President
new.x: Under Article 200 the Governor may assent, withhold, return or reserve a Bill, but has no pocket veto.

new.s: What is the maximum life of an ordinance?
new.x: The gap between sessions can be six months, and the ordinance lapses six weeks after reassembly.
